'''Endor - Death Star II Sealed''' is a sealed league format on [[GEMP]] built from [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]] Pre-Constructed Decks and [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] and Death Star II boosters. Its format definition uses the same set list as [[Open]].<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="sets" /><ref name="lib" /> GEMP's sealed league type ''Endor - Death Star II Sealed'' uses this format.<ref name="sealedtype" />

* '''Type:''' sealed deck (GEMP sealed league)
* '''Defined by:''' play.swccg.com format; league type from the Players Committee GEMP
* '''Card pool:''' Death Star II Pre-Constructed Decks plus Endor and Death Star II boosters, 40-card decks
* '''In use:''' unknown
* '''GEMP:''' ''Endor - Death Star II Sealed'' (<code>endor_dsII_sealed</code>) on play.swccg.com; on the Players Committee GEMP the league type ''Endor-Death Star II Sealed'' is played under the generic [[Sealed]] format<ref name="pc-slt" />

== Card pool ==
Players build decks from the product their sealed league gives them. A league has two series; a player who joins gets the product of every series that has started, and every player gets each later series' product when it starts.<ref name="nsld" /><ref name="slp" />

On play.swccg.com the league issues:<ref name="slp" />
* '''Series 1:''' 1 Death Star II Pre-Constructed Deck - Dark, 1 Death Star II Pre-Constructed Deck - Light, and 4 Endor Booster Packs (no random foils).<ref name="slp" />
* '''Series 2:''' 4 Death Star II Booster Packs.<ref name="slp" />
Each pre-constructed deck is a fixed 60-card deck. A Death Star II Booster Pack holds 7 commons, 3 uncommons and 1 rare; an Endor Booster Pack holds 5 commons, 3 uncommons and 1 rare, and in this league its rare is never replaced by a foil.<ref name="k-DeathStarIIDarkPreConstructedDeck" /><ref name="k-DeathStarIILightPreConstructedDeck" /><ref name="k-DeathStarIIBoosterPack" /><ref name="k-EndorBoosterPack" /> The full contents of each product are listed at [[GEMP sealed league products]].

The format definition uses the same set list as Open, so the product limits the pool. It sets a deck size of 40 cards and marks the format as not a game hall format, so it is played through its league rather than at open tables.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="sets" /><ref name="lib" />

=== Special rule ===
The GEMP format definitions list this special rule:<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="hall" />
* Once per game, a player may ▼ a unique battleground not already on table.

== History ==
The league type comes from the Players Committee GEMP code, which plays it under the generic [[Sealed]] format; play.swccg.com gave it its own format with the same name.<ref name="pc-slt" /><ref name="slt" /><ref name="gemp" />

The Players Committee's ''Alternate Format Tournament Guide'' lists paper formats on the same product: ''Death Star II Sealed'' (one Death Star II Pre-Constructed Deck), ''Death Star II Booster Draft'' (3 Endor and 3 Death Star II boosters), and a sealed version of the Battle of Endor environment, with a Death Star II Pre-Constructed Starter Deck and Endor and Death Star II boosters.<ref name="afg" /> Decipher's DecipherCon 2000 schedule had a Death Star II Sealed Booster Draft, and DecipherCon 2002 had a Death Star II / Endor Draft.<ref name="dcon2000" /><ref name="dcon2002" /> No source links the GEMP league to these events, and no league result in this format is recorded.
